parsed.summary: The file states the existence of a connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H on Fin q such that ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all large n. It adds that no proper 2-colouring has a side of maximum degree ≤ 2. It also states that Erdős's r-degenerate conjecture, ex(n,H)=O(n^{2−1/r}) for bipartite r-degenerate H, is false. The statements look faithful; the main caveat is that the first theorem carries an extra conjunct beyond the paper's Theorem 1.2, which makes it stronger.

glossary.plain: The neighbours of v inside the finite vertex set s, i.e. s ∩ N(v).
glossary.standard_concept: degree of v in the induced subgraph G[s]

glossary.plain: Every nonempty finite vertex set s has a vertex with at most r neighbours inside s.
glossary.standard_concept: r-degenerate graph (every nonempty subgraph has a vertex of degree ≤ r)
glossary.note: Using induced subgraphs on finsets is equivalent to using arbitrary subgraphs, since removing edges only lowers degrees.

glossary.plain: For every r>0 and every bipartite r-degenerate graph H on Fin q, ex(n,H)=O(n^{2−1/r}) as n→∞.
glossary.note: It relies on Mathlib's extremalNumber (max edges of an H-free simple graph on Fin n, with H-free meaning no subgraph copy) and Mathlib's IsBipartite (2-colourable). Both match the paper's ex(n,H) and bipartiteness.

lean_claims.plain: There exist q and a graph H on Fin q that is connected, bipartite and 2-degenerate. For every proper 2-colouring of H and each colour side, the maximum degree over that side exceeds 2. Moreover there are c, ε > 0 such that for all sufficiently large n, ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε}.
It is not true that for all r>0 and all bipartite r-degenerate H on Fin q, ex(n,H)=O(n^{2−1/r}).

paper_claims.plain: There exist a fixed connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H and constants c, ε > 0 with ex(n,H) ≥ c·n^{3/2+ε} for all sufficiently large n.
This disproves Erdős's conjecture that every bipartite r-degenerate graph has ex(n,H)=O(n^{2−1/r}), already at r=2.

coverage.why: It includes every conclusion of Theorem 1.2 and adds that neither colour class of any proper 2-colouring has maximum degree ≤ 2. This extra conjunct is not in the excerpt.
The negation of the formalized conjecture follows from the r=2 counterexample, because n^{3/2+ε} is not O(n^{3/2}).

flags.explanation: The conjunct that every side of every proper 2-colouring has maximum degree > 2 is extra relative to the paper's Theorem 1.2. It makes the theorem stronger and excludes the known cases of the conjecture. A side with no vertices has sup = 0, so the condition also forces both sides to be nonempty. Harmless, but not in the excerpt.

H is restricted to graphs on Fin q, which loses no generality up to isomorphism. The extremal number is Mathlib's, via H.Free (subgraph containment), matching the paper's definition. The exponent (2:ℕ)−1/r is cast to ℝ correctly, with no truncation problem since r>0.
